name: THE HOTEL LOBBY
note: Room 18, doc 20. ERRATA 34's asymmetry, and the room that sets the pattern: the back wall sits left of centre, the right-hand wall runs much longer, and the stair climbs it. THE FURNITURE IS DOC 26's, not the composition's -- a piano, two armchairs and a low table stood here before the writing landed, none of them was ever written, and a drawn object nobody wrote is a click with no answer. They came out; the settee, the stove, the spittoon and the clock went in. THE STAIRS is one object that is both a hotspot and the way upstairs, which is why its lines are on the exit rather than on a twin hotspot standing in the same place. materialIdentity: Worn blue-grey plush and tarnished brass (30d) -- the only interior in Act I with a BLUE cast. The assay office is achromatic cold; nothing else in Act I may go blue

hotspots.name: THE HOTEL CLERK
hotspots.note: He stands BEHIND the counter and is drawn before it, so the counter cuts him off at the chest. The rect covers only what clears the counter -- a hotspot over his hidden half would be a click on a man who is not visibly there. Doc 27 gives this character a tree and no examine layer. The hotspot is marked stub for the reason the word already means in this repo: the thing exists so the interaction works and its LOOK and LISTEN lines are honestly absent rather than invented. Three characters x two verbs x three variants is eighteen lines nobody has written, and check-examine-lines names them on every run until somebody does.

LOOK_AT.say: My name, spelled in a way it has never previously been spelled, in a hand of tremendous confidence.
repeat: Forty-one names. I have read all of them and I do not know one.
Mine is the last, and it is spelled in a way I have not previously encountered.
Nothing.
Nothing. It is a list of people who are elsewhere.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is the register. It stays on the desk and the desk stays where it is.

LOOK_AT.say: Forty keys. Four of them are out. The hotel is one-tenth occupied and charges as though it were not.
repeat: Four out of forty. The four are not near each other.
Number nineteen is mine. I have looked at it more than a man should look at a key.
Nothing.
Brass on wood, faintly, when the door goes.

overrides.PICK_UP: One of those is mine and the other thirty-nine are a matter for the management.

LOOK_AT.say: An engraving of the Bay of Naples, in a hotel lobby, in a mining camp, four hundred miles from a paved road. Somebody carried this here on purpose.
repeat: The Bay of Naples, in a mining camp, four hundred miles from a paved road.
It is hung too high, which suggests it was hung by somebody who did not want it looked at closely.
Nothing.
Nothing. It is a long way from home and so am I, and only one of us is framed.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is hung too high for a man who has not been invited to touch it.

LOOK_AT.say: A lobby clock. It disagrees with the Registrar's clock by nineteen minutes and neither has ever been challenged.
repeat: Nineteen minutes off the Registrar's, and neither has ever been challenged.
It is slow. In this town that is nearly an act of kindness.

LISTEN_TO.say: Ticking. Slightly slow. I am not going to say anything.
repeat: Ticking. Slow.
Ticking. I am not going to say anything.

overrides.USE: I have been asked not to.

LOOK_AT.say: Brass, and emptied. In a hotel lobby this counts as gentility.
repeat: It has been moved twice since this morning and it is still in the wrong place.
There is a ring on the carpet where it used to be and a ring where it is.
Nothing.
Nothing. We have both been spared.

LOOK_AT.say: A parlour stove with a nickel rail, polished. It is the only thing in this building anyone has spent an afternoon on.
repeat: Unlit. It has been unlit since I arrived, in a lobby with a rail for drying gloves.
The rail is for drying gloves. Nobody in Consolation owns gloves.
Nothing.
Nothing at all.

overrides.OPEN: Cold, and empty, and it has been both for some time.

LOOK_AT.say: A settee in worn blue plush, gone shiny at both arms and nowhere in the middle.
repeat: Two men have sat at either end of this for years and neither has moved to the centre.
It is the only comfortable thing I have seen since the coach, and the coach was not comfortable.
Nothing.
Nothing. Nobody is sitting on it and nobody is going to.

overrides.USE: I have sat on it. That is what happened next.

LOOK_AT.say: The door out onto Main Street, with a bell that does not work and a mat that has given up.
repeat: The bell is a formality. Everybody who comes in is already known.
Daylight, past it. It is always brighter than I remember.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street. Boots on the boardwalk.
repeat: Boots. Two men, and neither of them is coming in.
Nothing. It has gone quiet out there, which happens about four.

LOOK_AT.say: Stairs to the rooms, carpeted for the first four treads and bare above that. The carpet ran out.
repeat: Somebody measured wrong, or somebody ran out of money on the fifth tread.
The bare treads are worn more than the carpeted ones. Everyone is going up.

LISTEN_TO.say: Somebody on the landing, not moving. There is always somebody on the landing not moving.
repeat: Still there.
Boards. Two rooms, both occupied, neither talking.

entrances.note: In off the street, at the near end of the lobby with the desk ahead.
Down the stair, which climbs the long right-hand wall.

lightSources.note: The desk lamp. One oil lamp against a cool field, per errata 30d, with 33a's dark collar around it.
